paragraphs: Rav Huna bar Yehudah said …; Resh Lakish said: Sotah 41a; Yoma 70a. It requires examination why it put Rav Huna son of Rav Yehudah before Resh Lakish, who preceded him. Also Shabbat 109b. Perhaps this Yehudah was Rabbi Chiyya the Great’s son; yet he was in Rava’s time. He said to Rav Yehudah: Ketubbot 21a; see above, Rav Chiyya bar Yehudah. Mar Yehudah visited him: Eruvin 24a. He reported Rabbi Yitzchak, who reported Rabbi Yochanan: beginning of chapter Tefillat HaShachar. He reported Rabbi Menachem, who reported Rabbi Ammi: Berakhot 8a. Rav Huna son of Rav Yehudah said in Rav Nachman’s name, in Shmuel’s name: Pesachim 40, end of side b. He raised an objection to Rava: Niddah 46a; Zevachim 73b. He visited Rava’s house: Berakhot 52b; Pesachim 103a. He said to Rava: Nedarim 19b; Zevachim 6a, 91a. He visited the house of Avyoni and came before Rava: Bava Kamma 117a. Rav Huna son of Rav Yehudah stated a teaching before Rava: Pesachim 12a. He reported Rav Sheshet: Ketubbot 63b; Yoma 25, beginning of side a; Eruvin 26b. Bar Yehudah: Sotah 41a; Menachot 88b, 39a. There, “Rav Huna said in Rav Sheshet’s name” should read “Rav Huna bar Yehudah said in Rav Sheshet’s name”; newer Talmud editions did not correct it. In Shabbat 24a, Rav Sheshet said to him. “Shmuel’s student”: requires examination—where does he derive it? It also requires examination that he lived in Rav Yehudah’s and Rava’s days, unless there were two.
